第 19 章 Don't Be the S--- Umbrella别当挡屎伞

Jeff Foster / 杰夫·福斯特

— 第 63 页 —

When I first became an engineering manager, I saw my goal as protecting the team. I'd heroically take the flak from more senior managers, disgruntled salespeople, and field angry questions from support. I'd do everything I could to ensure that the team spent as much time as possible coding. I'd insulate the team from reality, protect them from outside harmful intent and basically just be a s--- umbrella. It's not glamorous work, but it's what a manager does, right?

刚做工程经理时，我把目标看作保护团队。我英勇地承受来自更高级经理的批评、不满的销售人员的指责、支持部门的愤怒质问。我尽我所能确保团队花尽可能多的时间写代码。我把团队和现实隔离开，保护他们免受外部恶意，基本上就是当一把「挡屎伞」。这工作不光鲜，但经理不就是干这个的吗？

Not right at all. This is not what an engineering manager should do! By insulating the team, I was putting myself under tremendous amounts of stress. After a few months, this job wasn't enjoyable any more. There's only so many calls you can take late at night before it takes its toll. It's easy to accept that this is the only way—that's why managers get paid the big bucks, isn't it?

大错特错。这不是工程经理该做的！通过隔离团队，我把自己置于巨大的压力之下。几个月后，这份工作就不再有趣了。深夜接电话总有个限度，之后就会付出代价。人们很容易接受这是唯一的方式——所以经理才拿高薪嘛，对吧？

So, what's wrong with being an umbrella?

那么，当伞有什么问题？

First, it fails for you, the manager, because you are putting yourself under unnecessary stress. You are not a superhero and eventually all that external pressure is going to adversely affect you.

第一，它对你——经理——是失败的，因为你把自己置于不必要的压力之下。你不是超级英雄，最终所有外部压力都会对你产生不利影响。

Second (and far more important), it fails for every single person on your team. By being the umbrella, you are actively harming the team's development. You are shielding the team from the reality of the project and stifling the personal development of team members.

第二（也是重要得多的），它对你团队里的每个人都是失败的。通过当伞，你正在 actively 损害团队的发展。你在把团队和项目现实隔离开，压抑团队成员的个人发展。

What should you do, instead?

那你应该做什么？

In my opinion, one of the most important things you can do as a manager is be transparent with your team. Don't be an umbrella, be a context provider.

在我看来，作为经理你能做的最重要的事情之一就是对团队透明。不要当伞，要当上下文提供者。

— 第 64 页 —

At first, this feels counterintuitive. My team is populated by engineers, they don't care about all of these "politics." This isn't true—the days of an engineer putting headphones on and writing code all day are gone. Engineers aren't measured on the number of lines they write, it's all about the business value. Providing the context in which they are operating is the most effective way to help them increase their value to the business and support their personal development.

一开始这感觉反直觉。我的团队都是工程师，他们不关心这些「政治」。这不是真的——工程师戴上耳机写一整天代码的日子已经一去不复返了。工程师不是用写了多少行代码来衡量的，一切都关于业务价值。提供他们运作的上下文是帮他们提高对业务的价值、支持他们个人发展的最有效方式。

This isn't about abdicating your responsibilities as a manager. It doesn't mean just acting as a filter. It means that you are constantly providing the team with a realistic understanding of the context they are operating in and involving your team in coming up with solutions.

这不是说放弃你作为经理的责任。不是说只是当过滤器。而是说你不断为团队提供他们运作的现实上下文理解，并让团队参与提出解决方案。

For example, I remember one time when marketing contacted my team in a fluster because there was a major conference in a few months and it didn't look like we'd get a release done by then. The naive approach to pass this onto the team would be to just let everyone know that we have a deadline and they should type faster (that's how things get shipped quicker, right?). The context provider approach is to invite marketing to talk to the team, help it get a deeper understanding of the problem and collaboratively come up with a better option. For the case I just mentioned, an engineer on the team made the breakthrough by reframing the problem—we don't need to release a new feature, we just need to demo it. The context reframed the problem and the team came up with a better solution.

举个例子，我记得有一次市场部慌慌张张联系我的团队，因为几个月后有个重要会议，看起来我们到那时候完不成发布。把这个传给团队的天真做法就是告诉大家我们有个截止日期、打字快点（东西就是这样变快的，对吧？）。上下文提供者的做法是邀请市场部和团队聊聊，帮团队更深入理解问题，共同想出更好的方案。就我刚才提到的情况，团队里一个工程师通过重新定义问题取得了突破——我们不需要发布新功能，只需要演示它。上下文重新定义了问题，团队想出了更好的解决方案。

By being a context provider, you can enable your team to show you their expertise. I'm a firm believer that the best people to make decisions are those closest to the problem. By giving context to the engineers on your team, you're setting them up for success and future development.

通过当上下文提供者，你能让团队展示他们的专业能力。我坚信做决策最好的人是离问题最近的人。通过给团队工程师提供上下文，你在为他们的成功和未来发展铺路。

In short, don't be a s--- umbrella: provide context, listen, and enable your team to grow.

简而言之，不要当挡屎伞：提供上下文，倾听，让团队成长。
